mainTopic: How מלקות is carried out, רב ששת's סמוכין teachings, and the new משנה that lashes free a person from כרת
overview: The גמרא explains why the person being flogged has his clothes torn: the Torah calls him 'נקלה,' debased. רב ששת then gives four teachings in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, each learned from neighboring פסוקים (סמוכין). These cover the calf-hide strap, the יבמה and the מוכה שחין, contempt for the מועדים, and לשון הרע with false testimony. Next the גמרא goes through the details of the משנה about מלקות: donkey-hide side straps, an adjustable strap, one third of the lashes in front and two thirds behind, and a doubled strap learned from והפילו. It also discusses who may give the lashes, how the judges read and count, and the rule that no extra blow may be added. It then explains when soiling himself frees the person from more lashes, and שמואל's rule that a man who runs away from בית דין is exempt. Finally a new משנה teaches, in the name of רבי חנניה בן גמליאל, that lashes free a person from כרת. רבי שמעון begins a proof of his own, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why are the clothes torn before flogging?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule that the attendant tears the clothes of the person being flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason the clothes are torn?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה says the attendant tears the person's clothes before giving מלקות. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule but not the reason. The גמרא wants a source in the Torah for treating the person this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה
Lashes given by בית דין (the topic of this chapter)

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the משנה's rule that the attendant tears the clothes of the one being flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source or reason for tearing the clothes of the person being flogged

steps.title: Because the Torah says he is 'debased'
steps.stepSummary: The reason is the word 'נקלה' (debased) in the flogging פסוק. Tearing his clothes is part of that debasement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the word 'debased.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with one word from the Torah: 'נקלה,' debased. The Torah expects the flogging to humble the person, so his clothes are torn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about מלקות says 'and your brother shall be debased before you.' Tearing the clothes and exposing the body is part of how that debasement happens. So the rule in the משנה comes straight from a word in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Because of 'debased.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:3

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם ״נִקְלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word נקלה in דברים 25:3 shows the person is meant to be debased, which tearing his clothes accomplishes
steps.whatToRemember: Tearing the clothes before מלקות comes from the Torah's word 'נקלה,' meaning the person is debased.

steps.title: The flogging strap is made of calf hide
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, learns that the strap comes from a calf. The reason is that the flogging פסוק sits right next to the פסוק about an ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: How do we know the strap is from a calf? Because it is written 'Forty he shall flog him,' and right next to it, 'Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. רב ששת brings a source showing the מלקות strap is made from calf leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method here is סמוכין: two פסוקים placed next to each other teach about each other. The flogging פסוק is followed by a פסוק about an ox. So the strap used for flogging comes from that kind of animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And right next to it is written (the basis of סמוכין)
Learning a law from two פסוקים that sit next to each other

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
From where do we know that the strap is from a calf?
As it is written: 'Forty he shall flog him,'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:3

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:4. The ox in the next פסוק points to cattle hide for the strap.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מִנַּיִן לִרְצוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the torn clothes to another detail of מלקות: what the strap is made of
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלקות strap is made of calf hide, learned from the ox פסוק placed next to the flogging פסוק
steps.whyThisMatters: This step also introduces the method of סמוכין, which the next three teachings use as well.

steps.title: A יבמה is not forced to marry a brother-in-law with boils
steps.stepSummary: Using the same ox פסוק, which is followed by the יבום section, רב ששת teaches that we do not force a יבמה into יבום with a מוכה שחין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: How do we know that a יבמה who comes before a brother-in-law afflicted with boils is not 'muzzled'? Because it is written 'Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes,' and right next to it, 'When brothers dwell together.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a second teaching with the same method. A widow whose brother-in-law has a skin disease is not forced into יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'do not muzzle' פסוק now works as the first half of a pair. Next to it comes the יבום section. So 'do not muzzle' carries over to the יבמה: we do not silence her objection and force her to marry this man.

keyTerms.meaning: A childless widow who is tied to her late husband's brother for יבום
Came to (became tied to) a certain brother-in-law
A man afflicted with boils (a painful skin disease)
Muzzle; here, silence her and force her

steps.confusionAlert: 'Muzzle' is not literal here. It means we do not shut down her complaint and force her into יבום.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיבָמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לִפְנֵי מוּכֵּה שְׁחִין,
phrases.english: From where do we know that a yevama who came before one afflicted with boils
phrases.notes: 'Came before' means the brother-in-law she is now tied to for יבום is this man with boils.

phrases.english: is not muzzled?
phrases.notes: We don't silence her objection. She is not forced to marry him.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes,'

phrases.aramaic: וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ ״כִּי יֵשְׁבוּ אַחִים יַחְדָּו וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and right next to it: 'When brothers dwell together, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5, the start of the יבום section.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מִנַּיִן לִיבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second סמוכין teaching from the same speaker, reusing the ox פסוק from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה tied to a brother-in-law with boils is not forced into יבום

steps.title: Treating the Festivals with contempt is like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: A third סמוכין teaching: the ban on molten gods is followed by the מצוה of פסח. So disrespecting the מועדים is compared to עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: Anyone who treats the Festivals with contempt is as if he serves idols, as it is written 'Molten gods you shall not make for yourself,' and right next to it, 'The festival of Matzot you shall keep.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a third teaching, this time a strong warning: belittling the Festivals is treated like idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the pair of פסוקים comes from שמות, not דברים. The ban on idols sits right next to the מצוה of keeping פסח. That closeness shows how seriously the תורה takes honoring the מועדים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who treats with contempt, belittles

steps.whatToRemember: Treating the מועדים with contempt is compared to עבודה זרה, because the two פסוקים sit side by side in שמות 34:17–18.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
Anyone who treats the Festivals with contempt
is as if he worships idols,
as it is written: 'Molten gods you shall not make for yourself,'
phrases.notes: שמות 34:17

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'The festival of Matzot you shall keep.'
phrases.notes: שמות 34:18

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: כׇּל הַמְבַזֶּה אֶת הַמּוֹעֲדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third teaching in the same series, now from different פסוקים and moving away from מלקות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who treats the Festivals with contempt is considered as if he worships idols

steps.title: Speakers of evil talk and false witnesses deserve to be thrown to the dogs
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, teaches through סמוכין that speaking or accepting לשון הרע, and giving false testimony, make a person fit to be thrown to the dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: anyone who speaks evil talk, anyone who accepts evil talk, and anyone who gives false testimony deserves to be thrown to the dogs. The פסוק says 'Throw it to the dog,' and right next to it, it says 'Do not accept a false report.' We can also read that word as 'Do not spread' a false report.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a fourth teaching from רב ששת using סמוכין, meaning two פסוקים that sit side by side. He links the end of one פסוק about dogs to the very next פסוק about false reports.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dog פסוק ends one section and 'לא תשא שמע שוא' begins the next, so the two are read together. The word תשא covers accepting a false report, and the rest of that פסוק warns against being a false witness. Reading it as תשיא, 'cause to carry,' also adds the person who spreads the report.

keyTerms.meaning: Evil talk; saying negative things about others
Placed right next to it (in the תורה)
Read it also as; reading a word a second way

steps.whatToRemember: This closes רב ששת's series of סמוכין teachings: the calf strap, the יבמה and the מוכה שחין, the מועדים, and now לשון הרע and false witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
Anyone who speaks evil talk,
and likewise one who accepts evil talk,
and anyone who gives false testimony –
deserves to be thrown to the dogs,
as it is written: 'To the dog you shall throw it,'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:30

phrases.aramaic: וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ ״לֹא תִשָּׂא שֵׁמַע שָׁוְא וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: and right next to it: 'You shall not accept a false report, etc.'
phrases.notes: שמות 23:1. The rest of the פסוק warns against being a false witness.

phrases.english: Read into it also: 'You shall not spread.'
phrases.notes: Same letters, different vowels. תשיא means making others 'carry' the report, so it covers the one who speaks it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further teaching in the same series of סמוכין teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking or accepting לשון הרע, and false testimony, make a person fit to be thrown to the dogs.

steps.title: The two side straps are made of donkey hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's two extra straps and cites a ברייתא saying they are made of donkey hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'and two straps.' A ברייתא teaches: they are made from a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next words of the משנה, the two straps, and says what they are made of. This sets up the next step, which explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that the main strap comes from a calf. Now we learn that the two side straps come from a donkey.

phrases.english: 'And two straps, etc.'
A ברייתא taught: they are of a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁתֵּי רְצוּעוֹת וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the series of סמוכין teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two side straps are made of donkey hide.

steps.title: The ox and the donkey punish the one who ignores his Master
steps.stepSummary: A Galilean's teaching on ישעיהו explains the ox and donkey straps: animals that know their master's trough punish a person who does not know his Master.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what a certain Galilean taught before רב חסדא: 'The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's trough, but Israel does not know.' The Holy One said: Let the one who knows its master's trough come and punish the one who does not know his Master's trough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason, based on a פסוק, why the straps come from an ox (the calf) and a donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק praises the ox and the donkey for being loyal to their owner, and blames Israel for not being loyal to ה׳. So a sinner, who ignored his Master, is struck with straps from those loyal animals.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him punish / collect payment

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains both animals at once. The calf strap from step 3 matches the 'ox,' and the donkey straps match the 'donkey.'

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְדָרֵישׁ הָהוּא גָּלִילָאָה עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: As a certain Galilean taught before Rav Chisda:
'The ox knows its owner,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:3

phrases.english: and the donkey its master's trough,
Israel does not know, etc.'
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Let the one who recognizes its master's trough come,

phrases.aramaic: וְיִפָּרַע מִמִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר אֵבוּס בְּעָלָיו.
phrases.english: and punish the one who does not recognize his Master's trough.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְדָרֵישׁ הָהוּא גָּלִילָאָה עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the donkey-hide rule
steps.raayaObject: That the straps are made of donkey (and ox) hide
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 1:3, as taught by a Galilean before רב חסדא

steps.title: אביי: each person gets a strap made for his size
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's measurements, אביי concludes that a strap is made to match each person's back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'its handle is a טפח, etc.' אביי said: Learn from this that for each person, we make a strap that fits his back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the strap measurements from the משנה, and אביי draws a practical conclusion from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires the end of the strap to reach the top of the person's stomach. People are different sizes, so אביי reasons that each person needs his own strap.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; conclude from this

phrases.english: 'Its handle is a handbreadth, etc.'
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say the strap must reach the top of his stomach. That is what אביי is working from.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from it

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל חַד וְחַד לְפוּם גַּבֵּיהּ עָבְדִינַן לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: that for each and every one, we make it according to his back.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָדָהּ טֶפַח וְכוּ׳. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A separate strap is made to fit each person's size.

steps.title: רבא: that would mean far too many straps
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that אביי's approach would force the court to keep a huge number of straps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, they would need very many straps!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's conclusion on practical grounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every body size needed its own strap, the court would have to keep a whole stock of them. That is not sensible, so רבא does not accept the idea.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן נַפֵּישׁ לְהוּ רְצוּעוֹת טוּבָא!
phrases.english: If so, they would have a great many straps!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's conclusion
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that each person gets a strap made for him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would be impractical: the court would need countless straps.

steps.title: רבא: one strap with loops that can be adjusted
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests that the strap has loops, so it can be made shorter or longer to fit each person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It has loops. When he wants, he ties it up with them, and when he wants, he loosens it.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of אביי's view, רבא explains how a single strap can fit everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule that the strap must fit the person still stands. But it is done by adjusting one strap with loops, not by making many straps.
steps.whatToRemember: The strap must reach each person correctly, and this is done with one adjustable strap.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It has loops;
when he wants, he ties it up with them,
when he wants, he loosens it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אַבְקָתָא אִית לַיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's view after רבא's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each person needs his own strap.
steps.terutzMaskana: One strap with loops is adjusted for each person.

steps.title: What is the source for where the lashes are given?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule: one third of the lashes in front, two thirds behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'They flog him, etc.' From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about how the lashes are divided and asks for its source. This sets up רב כהנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a third of the lashes go on the front of his body and two thirds on his back. The גמרא wants to know where the תורה hints at this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: 'They flog him, etc.'
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: one third in front of him and two thirds behind him.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְקִין אוֹתוֹ וְכוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source for one third of the lashes in front and two thirds behind

steps.title: רב כהנא: 'his wickedness' teaches one part in front, two behind
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reads the flogging פסוק 'strike him before him according to his wickedness' as one portion of wickedness in front of him, with the other two portions given behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The פסוק says, 'The judge shall make him lie down and strike him before him, according to his wickedness, by number.' One 'wickedness' in front of him, and two 'wickednesses' behind him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question by reading the words of the flogging פסוק closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא reads 'strike him before him according to his wickedness' as one portion of wickedness in front of him. The other two portions are given behind him. That makes three portions: one in front and two behind.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall make him lie down
Wickedness; here, one portion of lashes

steps.confusionAlert: The 'one' and 'two' are not single lashes. They are portions: one third of the lashes in front and two thirds behind.
steps.whatToRemember: One third of the lashes go on the front of the body and two thirds on the back, learned from 'לפניו כדי רשעתו.'

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
As the verse states: 'And the judge shall make him lie down'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2

phrases.english: and strike him before him
according to his wickedness, by number' –
one wickedness from in front of him,
two wickednesses from behind him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 25:2: 'לפניו כדי רשעתו' means one portion of wickedness in front of him. The remaining two portions are given behind him.

steps.title: The strap is doubled, learned from והפילו
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה, רב חסדא in the name of רבי יוחנן derives from the word והפילו that the strap used for מלקות is folded double.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He does not flog him...' etc. רב חסדא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: How do we know the strap is doubled? Because the פסוק says 'והפילו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line in the משנה about the position of the person being flogged. רבי יוחנן uses the same פסוק to teach a new detail: the strap is folded double.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of והפילו is 'he shall make him lie down,' which is why the person is flogged bent over. רבי יוחנן reads the word as hinting at doubling, so the strap must be folded over.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall make him lie down'; here also read as a hint to doubling

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'He does not flog him,' etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה said he is not flogged standing or sitting, only bent over.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
From where do we know that the strap is doubled?
As it says: 'And he shall make him lie down.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2. The word sounds like an Aramaic word for 'double', so it hints at a folded strap.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִנַּיִן לִרְצוּעָה שֶׁהִיא מוּכְפֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and adds a new detail about the strap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strap used for מלקות is doubled, learned from the word והפילו.

steps.title: But that word is needed for its own plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the word והפילו is already used to teach that the person is flogged lying or bent over, so how can it also teach about the strap?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word is needed for its own plain meaning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's source. The word והפילו already has a job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that a word already used for its plain lesson cannot automatically teach a second lesson. The plain lesson here is the bent-over position from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself, for its own plain meaning

phrases.english: But he needs it for its own plain meaning!
phrases.notes: The plain meaning is that the person being flogged must lie or bend down.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְגוּפֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of והפילו to teach that the strap is doubled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already used for the position of the person being flogged, so it is not free to teach something else.

steps.title: The unusual word teaches both lessons
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah only wanted to teach the position, it could have written יטיהו ('bend him'). Choosing והפילו shows it teaches two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק write 'יטיהו' (bend him). Why does it say 'הפילו'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The Torah picked a special word on purpose, so it carries both lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A simpler word, יטיהו, would have been enough for the position. The extra choice of הפילו, which hints at doubling, teaches about the strap as well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall bend him', the simpler word the Torah could have used

steps.whatToRemember: והפילו teaches two things: the person is flogged bent over, and the strap is doubled.

phrases.english: If so, let the פסוק write 'bend him'.
Why does it say 'make him lie down'?
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לִכְתּוֹב קְרָא ״יַטֵּיהוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra or unusual wording in the פסוק allows a second lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word was needed only for the bent-over position.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the Torah chose הפילו instead of יטיהו, it teaches both the position and the doubled strap.

steps.title: Who may be appointed to give lashes
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about the attendant striking, a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת. The רבנן appoint only weak, learned חזנין. רבי יהודה allows even unlearned, strong ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The one who strikes strikes with his hand.' The Rabbis taught: We appoint as attendants only people who are weak in strength and great in knowledge. רבי יהודה says: Even people lacking knowledge and great in strength.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about which attendants the court may choose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן want someone learned who will follow the rules exactly, and they accept that he is weak. רבי יהודה allows someone strong even if he is not learned.

keyTerms.meaning: Court attendants (here, the ones who give the lashes)

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'The one who strikes strikes with his hand.'
The Rabbis taught: We do not appoint attendants
except those weak in strength and great in knowledge.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even those lacking knowledge and great in strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּכֶּה מַכֶּה בְּיָדוֹ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַעֲמִידִין חַזָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן require weak, learned attendants. רבי יהודה also allows strong, unlearned ones.

steps.title: רבא supports רבי יהודה from the warning not to add
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the Torah's warning 'he shall not add' makes sense only if the attendant might not know the rules. That fits רבי יהודה, who allows unlearned attendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense to rule like רבי יהודה, because it is written 'He shall not add... lest he add.' If you say we appoint people lacking knowledge, that is why the Torah needs to warn him. But if you say only very learned people, does the Torah need to warn them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof from a פסוק to show that רבי יהודה's view is more reasonable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A learned attendant already knows not to give extra lashes, so a warning would be pointless. The fact that the Torah warns suggests the attendant may be unlearned, as רבי יהודה says.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִסְתַּבְּרָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: It makes sense to follow Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is written: 'He shall not add... lest he add.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:3

phrases.english: It works well if you say people lacking knowledge are appointed:
that is why he needs to be warned.
But if you say only people great in knowledge are appointed,
would they need to be warned?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Weighs in on the מחלוקת of step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that unlearned attendants may be appointed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's warning 'לא יוסיף... פן יוסיף' would be unneeded for learned attendants.

steps.title: The רבנן: you warn only someone who is already careful
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבא's proof. A warning works best on someone who is already careful, so the warning fits a learned attendant too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis? They say: We only urge someone who is already eager.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן would answer רבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed a warning is needed only for someone who does not know the rules. The רבנן answer that warnings are given to people who already care, because they are the ones who will take them seriously. So the פסוק does not prove רבי יהודה right.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not settle the מחלוקת. It only shows that רבא's פסוק is not a forced proof for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? We only urge someone who is already eager.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: אֵין מְזָרְזִין אֶלָּא לַמְזוֹרָז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the פסוק. It does not prove the רבנן correct.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed warnings are given only to those who lack knowledge. In fact, warnings are given even to those already careful.

steps.title: Lift with two hands, strike with one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the attendant raises the strap with both hands but strikes with one hand, so the blow comes from his own effort.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: When he lifts the strap, he lifts with both hands. When he strikes, he strikes with one hand, so that the blow comes from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's words 'strikes with his hand'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said he strikes with his hand. The ברייתא clarifies that he uses two hands only for lifting and one hand for the actual blow, so the strike comes from his own effort.

keyTerms.meaning: From himself, by his own effort

steps.whatToRemember: The strap is lifted with both hands but strikes with only one hand.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מַגְבִּיהַּ – מַגְבִּיהַּ בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו,
phrases.english: It was taught: When he lifts, he lifts with both his hands,
and when he strikes, he strikes with one hand,
so that it will come from him.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets, 'will come,' is the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מַגְבִּיהַּ – מַגְבִּיהַּ בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's phrase 'strikes with his hand' (step 17) and explains how it works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The attendant lifts the strap with both hands and strikes with one hand.

steps.title: Three judges share the jobs, and the reading matches the number of lashes
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about the reader, a ברייתא says the senior judge reads, the second counts, and the third says 'strike him.' The reader stretches or shortens his reading to fit the number of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the reader reads, etc.' The Rabbis taught: The greatest of the judges reads the פסוקים, the second counts the lashes, and the third says, 'Strike him!' When there are many lashes, the reader reads slowly. When there are few lashes, he reads quickly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the reader and brings a ברייתא. The ברייתא explains who does each job during the lashes and how the reading is timed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three judges each have their own job: reading, counting, and giving the order to strike. The reading is timed so that it starts and ends with the lashes. With many lashes the reader slows down, and with few lashes he speeds up.

keyTerms.meaning: The reader, who reads פסוקים aloud during the lashes

phrases.english: 'And the reader reads,' etc.
The Rabbis taught: the greatest of the judges reads,
the second counts,
and the third says: 'Strike him!'
When the lashes are many, he reads slowly,
when the lashes are few, he reads quickly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַקּוֹרֵא קוֹרֵא וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three judges divide the reading, counting, and command, and the reading is timed to fit the number of lashes.

steps.title: But the משנה says he goes back to the start of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the reading is always timed to fit, why does the משנה say the reader goes back to the beginning of the פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: he goes back to the beginning of the פסוק!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with the משנה. The משנה says the reader may run out of פסוקים and start again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reader always matches his speed to the lashes, he should never finish early. The משנה's rule about starting the פסוק again suggests the reading does not always fit exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes back to the beginning of the פסוק

phrases.english: But we learned:
He goes back to the beginning of the verse!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that the reading is timed to the lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reading always fits, there would be no need to go back to the start, yet the משנה says to go back.

steps.title: Matching is the ideal, and going back is the fallback
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה is to time the reading exactly. If the reader did not manage that and finished early, he goes back to the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה is to time it exactly. If he did not time it exactly, he goes back to the beginning of the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא and the משנה describe two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the ideal way: timing the reading so it ends with the lashes. The משנה describes what to do if the timing did not work out: start the פסוקים again. Both rules are true.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה is to time it exactly

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is to match the reading to the lashes. If the reading ends early, the reader starts it again.

phrases.english: The מצוה is to time it exactly,
and if he did not time it exactly,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling: אִם, 'if.'

phrases.english: he goes back to the beginning of the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוָה לְצַמְצֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the ideal way versus the fallback
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה seem to disagree about whether the reading must fit exactly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא gives the ideal, and the משנה gives what to do if the ideal was missed.

steps.title: Even a small extra blow is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that 'a great blow' alone would only forbid a big extra blow. The words 'he shall not add' teach that even a small extra blow is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'A great blow.' From this I only know that a great extra blow is forbidden. How do I know a small one is also forbidden? The פסוק says, 'He shall not add.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from the פסוק that any extra blow at all, even a weak one, is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions 'a great blow,' which could suggest that only a big extra blow is forbidden. But 'he shall not add' is a general ban on adding, so even a light extra blow is included.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'a great blow,'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:3

phrases.english: I have only a great blow;
from where do I know a small blow?
The verse says: 'He shall not add.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מַכָּה רַבָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא about the lashes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding any extra blow, even a weak one, is forbidden because of 'he shall not add.'

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say 'a great blow'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'he shall not add' already forbids every extra blow, the ברייתא asks what the words 'a great blow' come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'a great blow'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up question. It sets up the next step, which gives a new use for the words 'a great blow.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'he shall not add' covers every case, the words 'a great blow' seem extra. The Torah does not waste words, so they must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק say this? (these words seem extra)

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מַכָּה רַבָּה״?
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say 'a great blow'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is left for the words 'a great blow' to teach after step 24
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'a great blow' teach, now that they are not needed for the ban

steps.title: The first lashes must be strong
steps.stepSummary: 'A great blow' teaches that the lashes the person is supposed to get must be given with full strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches about the first lashes, that they must be a great blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the words 'a great blow' teach how the real lashes must be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The first lashes' are the lashes the person is actually supposed to get, the ones before any forbidden extra. Those must be full-strength blows. So the פסוק teaches two things: the real lashes must be strong, and no extra blow may be added.

keyTerms.meaning: The first lashes (the ones he is supposed to get)

phrases.english: It teaches about the first ones,
phrases.notes: He means the lashes the person is supposed to receive, before any forbidden extra.

phrases.english: that they are a great blow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִימֵּד עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'A great blow' teaches that the required lashes are given with full strength.

steps.title: Three opinions on what kind of sullying frees him from more lashes
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about נתקלקל, a ברייתא brings a three-way מחלוקת. רבי מאיר says only רעי frees a man or a woman. רבי יהודה says רעי frees a man, and מים also free a woman. חכמים say either one frees both.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he sullied himself, etc.' The Rabbis taught: For both a man and a woman, רעי frees them but urine does not. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: a man is freed by רעי, and a woman even by urine. חכמים say: both a man and a woman are freed by either רעי or urine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about someone who sullied himself during the lashes. It brings a ברייתא with three opinions about which kind of sullying stops the lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that רעי stops the lashes for a man. רבי מאיר says only רעי counts, even for a woman. רבי יהודה adds that urine is enough for a woman. חכמים say urine is enough for a man too.

keyTerms.meaning: He sullied himself during the lashes, which frees him from the rest

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מים' does not mean water. It means urine.

phrases.english: 'He sullied himself,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: if he sullies himself during the lashes, he gets no more lashes.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶחָד הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד הָאִשָּׁה
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: both the man and the woman

phrases.aramaic: בְּרֵיעִי וְלֹא בְּמַיִם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: with excrement and not with urine; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָאִישׁ בְּרֵיעִי, וְהָאִשָּׁה בְּמַיִם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the man with excrement, and the woman with urine.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד הָאִשָּׁה –
phrases.english: And the Sages say: both the man and the woman
whether with excrement or with urine.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְקַלְקֵל וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A three-way מחלוקת about whether רעי, urine, or both free a man or a woman from more lashes.

steps.title: Another ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה differently
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that רבי יהודה holds that both a man and a woman are freed by רעי. This seems to mean urine does not free a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, both a man and a woman are freed by רעי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction in what רבי יהודה said, between this ברייתא and the one just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, רבי יהודה says urine frees a woman. In this ברייתא, he mentions only רעי for both a man and a woman, which sounds like urine does not free a woman.

phrases.english: But it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
both the man and the woman, with excrement!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 27 quotes רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view in step 27 that urine frees a woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא mentions only רעי for both, which suggests urine does not free a woman.

steps.title: Both are equal regarding רעי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the second ברייתא only says that a man and a woman are the same regarding רעי. It does not deny that urine frees a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The two of them are equal regarding רעי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק solves the contradiction by explaining what the second ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא only teaches that רעי frees both a man and a woman. It says nothing against urine freeing a woman. So both ברייתות can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: The two of them are equal

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, רעי frees both a man and a woman from more lashes, and urine also frees a woman. The two ברייתות do not disagree.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The two of them are equal with excrement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִין בְּרֵיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the second ברייתא means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second ברייתא seemed to mean that only רעי frees a woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only says a man and a woman are equal regarding רעי. Urine still frees a woman.

steps.title: A bound man who runs away is let off
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if they tied a person up for מלקות and he ran away from בית דין, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If they tied him up for lashes and he ran away from the court, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new rule. If someone was already tied up to get lashes and he escaped from בית דין, we do not bring him back to be whipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gives no reason here. He only rules that once the man has fled, בית דין does not bring him back for the lashes. This rule now becomes the target of the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: They tied him up (to the post for lashes)
Exempt; he does not get the lashes

phrases.english: Shmuel said: If they tied him up,
and he ran away from the court, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּפָתוּהוּ, וְרָץ מִבֵּית דִּין – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the מחלוקת about נתקלקל to a new case where the person is freed: running away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man tied up for מלקות who runs away from בית דין is exempt.

steps.title: A snapped strap on the first lash does not free him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the strap snaps on the first lash, he is not let off. The גמרא asks: why not treat him like someone who ran away?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If he soiled himself, whether at the first lash or the second, they let him off. If the strap snapped at the second lash, they let him off. If it snapped at the first lash, they do not let him off. Why not? Let him be like one who ran away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge שמואל. In the ברייתא, a man whose strap snapped on the very first lash is still whipped, but according to שמואל that should count like running away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even running away before any lash frees a man, then a broken strap at the start should free him too. The ברייתא says it does not, so it seems to argue with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: He was disgraced, meaning he soiled himself

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If he was disgraced, whether at the first or at the second,
phrases.notes: He soiled himself, the case of נתקלקל from the משנה. "First" and "second" mean the first and second lash.

phrases.english: they let him off.
If the strap snapped at the second, they let him off;
at the first, they do not let him off.
Why? Let him be like one who ran away!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that running away before the lashes frees him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If running away with no lashes frees a man, a snapped strap on the first lash should free him as well. The ברייתא says it does not.

steps.title: Running away is different from a snapped strap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in שמואל's case the man actually ran away, but with the snapped strap he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There he ran away; here he did not run away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. Once a man has actually escaped, we do not drag him back, but a man who is still standing there just gets whipped with a new strap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are not the same. Running away is a real escape, but a broken strap is just a pause. So the ברייתא does not argue with שמואל.
steps.whatToRemember: Running away from בית דין frees a man from the lashes. A snapped strap on the first lash does not, because he never left.

phrases.english: There he ran away; here he did not run away.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם רָץ, הָכָא לָא רָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by telling the two cases apart.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A snapped strap before any lashes should be just like running away.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a man who actually escaped is let off. One who stayed is whipped with a new strap.

steps.title: Estimating ahead of time whether he will soil himself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if בית דין estimates he will soil himself from the lashes, they let him off. If he will only soil himself after leaving, they whip him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If they estimated that when he is whipped he will soil himself, they let him off. If they estimated that he will soil himself only when he leaves the court, they whip him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא explains how בית דין handles the risk of the person soiling himself. It depends on when that would happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the soiling would come during the lashes, the person is not whipped at all. If it would only happen later, after he leaves, it does not stop the lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: They estimated about him (how much he can take)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If they estimated about him
that when he is whipped he will soil himself, they let him off.
If they estimated that when he leaves the court he will soil himself,
they whip him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֲמָדוּהוּ לִכְשֶׁיִּלְקֶה קָלֶה – פּוֹטְרִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of נתקלקל and adds the case of estimating ahead of time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soiling expected during the lashes frees him. Soiling expected only after he leaves does not.

steps.title: Soiling before the lashes begin does not free him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that even if he soiled himself before any lash, they still whip him, because the פסוק speaks of disgrace that comes from the lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but even if he soiled himself at the very start, they whip him, as it says: "And strike him... and he will be disgraced." This means disgrace from the lashes, not one who was already disgraced in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further. Soiling himself before the lashes start does not free him, and it brings a פסוק to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, "and he will be disgraced" comes after "and strike him." So only disgrace caused by the striking frees him. Disgrace that happened earlier does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even more
At the start, before any lash

steps.whatToRemember: Only soiling caused by the lashes frees him. Soiling before the lashes or after leaving does not.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
even if he soiled himself at the start, they whip him,
as it says: "And strike him... and he will be disgraced,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2–3

phrases.english: and not one who was already disgraced in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא, אֲפִילּוּ קָלָה בַּתְּחִלָּה – מַלְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a further case and a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soiling before the lashes begin does not free him, because the פסוק links the disgrace to the striking.

steps.title: משנה: Lashes free a person from כרת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that anyone liable for כרת who got lashes is freed from כרת, because after the lashes he is called "your brother." This is the view of רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All those liable for כרת who were whipped are freed from their כרת, as it says: "And your brother will be disgraced before your eyes." Once he is whipped, he is like your brother. These are the words of רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that getting lashes removes the punishment of כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the whipped person "your brother." רבי חנניה בן גמליאל learns from this that his sin is forgiven and he is no longer cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: People liable for כרת (being cut off)
They are freed from their כרת

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that מלקות is not only a punishment. It also brings the person back fully into the community.

phrases.english: Mishnah: All those liable for karet who were whipped
are freed from their karet,
as it says: "And your brother will be disgraced before your eyes":
phrases.notes: דברים 25:3

phrases.english: once he is whipped, he is like your brother.
These are the words of Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת שֶׁלָּקוּ – נִפְטְרוּ יְדֵי כְּרִיתָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lashes free a person liable for כרת from his כרת.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: if a sin takes the soul, a מצוה gives it
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניה בן גמליאל argues that if one sin can cost a person his soul, then doing one מצוה should surely give him his soul.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנניה בן גמליאל said: If one who does one sin loses his soul for it, then one who does one מצוה, how much more so should his soul be given to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנניה בן גמליאל adds a reason to back up his view. He uses a קל וחומר comparing punishment with reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One sin is enough to bring כרת, losing the soul. Reward is stronger than punishment, so doing a מצוה should surely earn back his soul. This supports the idea that a sinner can be saved from כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: How much more so (a קל וחומר)
That his soul be given to him

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel said:
If one who does one sin
loses his soul for it,
then one who does one מצוה,
how much more so
should his soul be given to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מָה אִם הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אַחַת נוֹטֵל נַפְשׁוֹ עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same תנא adds a קל וחומר to back up his teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can be saved from losing his soul.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר: reward for a מצוה is greater than punishment for a sin.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns it from the same passage
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the idea can be learned from the same section of the תורה, and starts quoting the פסוק about souls being cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: It is learned from its own place, as it says: "And the souls that do them will be cut off..."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון begins his own proof straight from the פסוקים about כרת. He quotes the first פסוק, and the rest of his proof continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a קל וחומר, רבי שמעון wants to prove the point from the same passage that gives the punishment of כרת. Here he quotes the פסוק of the punishment, and he will pair it with another פסוק from that section.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from its own place (the same section)
And the souls will be cut off

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
It is learned from its own place,
phrases.notes: He means from the same passage in the תורה that talks about כרת for forbidden relationships.

phrases.english: as it says: "And the souls that do them will be cut off..."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29. His proof continues in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוּא לָמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source than רבי חנניה בן גמליאל's קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: The same idea that a person can be rewarded with his soul.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוקים in ויקרא 18, starting with 18:29.
